title: introduce preflight-sideline job and ci-hygiene-sweeper; split toolchain bootstrap
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation:
Reducing developer fatigue from noisy presubmit runs while keeping fast feedback for regressions. This PR introduces a lightweight "preflight-sideline" workflow that runs fast static checks and targeted smoke tests in parallel with the existing presubmit lanes, plus a ci-hygiene-sweeper tool that identifies stale devdeps, unused workflows, and expired runner labels. It also separates the monolithic 'toolchain bootstrap' manifest into stable runtime and ephemeral dev toolchain manifests so CI can fetch smaller images for presubmit fastpath.

What this PR does (summary):
- Add .github/workflows/preflight-sideline.yml: a fast, low-cost job that runs TypeScript typecheck, python-flake/black quick checks, and a small smoke harness against a cached toolchain image. Designed to run on push and PR concurrently but with lower concurrency and quiet notifications.
- Add tools/ci/sweeper.py: a scheduled script (weekly) that collects package.json/pipfile snapshots, flags devdeps not referenced in any package or scripts, and makes a maintenance report in Linear. The script supports a --dry-run mode and an enterprise flag to disable auto-suggestion edits.
- Split ci/toolchains/toolchain-manifests.yaml into ci/toolchains/runtime-manifest.yaml and ci/toolchains/devtools-manifest.yaml. The runtime manifest is used by nightly/integration pipelines; the devtools manifest is smaller and prioritized for presubmit.
- Minimal refactor of scripts/presubmit-wrapper.sh to honor PRELIGHT_FAST=true and early-exit for long-running steps when preflight-sideline already passed.
- Update docs/ci.md with rationale, opt-out flags, and examples for on-call/SE teams.
- Bump a handful of CI action pins (actions/checkout@v4 -> v4.1 pinned commit) and add an integration test that asserts preflight job completes within 120s on typical runner.

Checklist:
- [x] Add preflight-sideline workflow and runner labels
- [x] Implement ci-hygiene-sweeper with dry-run and report modes
- [x] Split toolchain manifests and update presubmit wrapper to prefer devtools manifest
- [x] Update docs and RELEASE_NOTES
- [x] Add unit tests for sweeper logic and a lightweight integration smoke test for preflight

Commits (high level):
- feat(ci): add preflight-sideline workflow and job templates
- feat(ci): introduce ci-hygiene-sweeper script and scheduler
- refactor(ci): split toolchain manifest into runtime/devtools
- chore(ci): pin actions and update bootstrap helper
- test(ci): add unit tests for sweeper and preflight smoke harness
- docs: document new workflow and opt-out flags in ci.md

Files touched (high level):
- .github/workflows/preflight-sideline.yml
- .github/workflows/ci-scheduler.yml (added weekly trigger for sweeper)
- tools/ci/sweeper.py (+ tests tools/ci/test_sweeper.py)
- ci/toolchains/runtime-manifest.yaml
- ci/toolchains/devtools-manifest.yaml
- scripts/presubmit-wrapper.sh
- docs/ci.md
- .github/actions/pinned-versions.json (minor pins)

Testing and CI behavior:
- Local unit tests: all passing (python pytest for sweeper; ts typecheck for preflight harness)
- CI: initial run showed build-image job failing due to stale base image tag. Updated manifest and re-ran; subsequent run passed.
- Preflight job is gated to quiet notifications: failed preflight will not send noise to #dev-notifications, it will create a single aggregated thread comment on the PR.

Review notes and decisions:
- Sweeper requires explicit opt-in (default dry-run). We debated auto-PR creation for devdep removals; decided against it for now to avoid churn. See comment thread below.
- The toolchain split intentionally keeps the runtime manifest stable to reduce image churn for longtests and integration pipelines. Devtools manifest is re-generated by the existing toolchain generation pipeline.
- Presubmit-wrapper early-exit behavior is conservative: it only skips long linters when PRELIGHT_FAST succeeded and the changed paths are limited to codegen/docs/infra files.

Migration plan:
- Roll out preflight-sideline as opt-in to teams for 1 week, then enable org-wide with a 48h rollback window controlled by feature flag in .github/ci-flags.yml.
- Schedule ci-hygiene-sweeper in the next maintenance window; start with dry-run reports to team leads for 2 weeks before enabling suggestions.

Related work:
- ENG-2374: presubmit feedback latency reduction
- ENG-2419: toolchain image fragmentation and cache sizes
- SUP-1423: support request from platform team to reduce presubmit noise

Potential risks and mitigations:
- Risk: preflight false-positives letting regressions slip. Mitigation: the preflight is advisory for now and cannot gate merges until +2 weeks of telemetry.
- Risk: sweeper suggestions remove needed devdeps. Mitigation: dry-run default and owner review required before edits.

Release notes:
"This release adds a low-noise preflight CI lane that provides fast feedback for common static errors, and a scheduled ci-hygiene-sweeper utility that surfaces stale dev dependencies and workflow clutter. The CI toolchain manifests are split to reduce presubmit image size. These changes reduce developer notifications and improve presubmit turnaround time."

CI telemetry summary (post-merge):
- Average presubmit runtime reduced by ~18% in canary org teams when PRELIGHT_FAST honored
- Preflight false-positive rate measured at 0.6% over first 48h (alerts created then triaged)
- Sweeper dry-run flagged ~42 packages across the org for manual review

review_comments: Evan Cho: Nice approach to reduce noise — can we make the preflight time budget configurable per team? Requested change: expose PRELIGHT_TIMEOUT in .github/ci-flags.yml.
Maya Patel (author): Added PRELIGHT_TIMEOUT with a reasonable default (120s). We can escalate to team overrides later.
Liam O'Connor: Sweeper looks useful but please add enterprise opt-out before any auto-PR work. Also add tests for patterns that detect scripts referencing devdeps.
Maya Patel (author): Sweeper has --enterprise-disable flag and added tests covering common npm/pip script patterns.
Priya Iyer: Approving pending one small doc clarification about rollback steps.
Maya Patel (author): Clarified rollback steps in docs/ci.md and added one-liner on how to revert the feature flag.
